key_insight: A classifier-chain multi-label model can recommend pathology tests from symptoms with very high accuracy, helping speed up pre-consultation diagnostic planning.
clinical_relevance: This could support clinicians by narrowing test choices faster and making symptom-to-test reasoning more transparent in busy or time-sensitive settings.
method: Trained multi-label classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest, using a Classifier Chain approach.
Compared model performance on a custom pathology dataset built from SOUTHERN.IML pathology data with expert input.
Used SHAP to explain which symptoms most influenced each test recommendation.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Logistic Regression with Classifier Chain achieved the highest overall accuracy (98.83%), while a Majority Voting ensemble had the best balance of precision (0.93), recall (0.85), and F1-score (0.89).
watch_item: Performance was reported from a specific dataset and workflow, so broader clinical use would need external validation and careful integration into physician decision-making.
